# What is Quarto?

Quarto is a publishing system that lets you combine text, code, and output into a single document.

**Why use Quarto?**

- Write analysis and explanation in one place
- Code runs and updates automatically when you render
- Export to HTML, PDF, Word, slides, websites
- All your assignments will be `.qmd` files rendered to `.html`
- Your final project will be a Quarto website

**The workflow:**

1. Write text and code in a `.qmd` file
2. Click "Render" (or Ctrl+Shift+K)
3. Quarto runs your code and produces a polished document

# Quarto Basics

## The YAML Header

Every Quarto document starts with a YAML header between `---` marks:

```yaml
---
title: "My Analysis"
author: "Your Name"
date: today
format: html
---
```

This controls the document's metadata and output format.

## Markdown Formatting

Quarto uses Markdown for text formatting:

- *italics* with `*italics*`
- **bold** with `**bold**`
- [links](https://quarto.org) with `[text](url)`
- Create sections with `#`, `##`, `###`

### Lists

Bullet points:

- First item
- Second item
- Third item

Numbered lists:

1. First step
2. Second step
3. Third step

### Math

Use LaTeX for equations. Inline math: $y = mx + b$

Display equations:

$$
\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i
$$

### Images

Include images from your project folder:

```markdown
![Caption text](image.png){width="50%"}
```

![Shakira knows what's up](shakira.jpeg){width="30%"}

### Tables

Create tables by hand:

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|----------|----------|----------|
| A        | B        | C        |
| D        | E        | F        |

### Footnotes

Add footnotes like this.[^1]

[^1]: This is the footnote text.

# Code in Quarto

The real power of Quarto is integrating code with your writing.

## Code Chunks

Insert R code in "chunks" that look like this:

````
```{{r}}
# Your R code here
mean(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5))
```
````

When you render, the code runs and the output appears in your document.

## Example: Running Code

```{r}
# This code will run when you render
x <- c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50)
mean(x)
```

## Chunk Options

Control how chunks behave with options:

```
#| echo: true       # Show the code in output
#| echo: false      # Hide the code, show only results
#| eval: false      # Show code but don't run it
#| warning: false   # Suppress warning messages
#| message: false   # Suppress messages
```

## Example: Hidden Code

Sometimes you want to show results but hide the code:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = hp, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Horsepower vs Fuel Efficiency")
```

The plot appears, but readers don't see the code that made it.

## Inline Code

Reference values directly in your text using inline code.

```{r}
n_cars <- nrow(mtcars)
avg_mpg <- round(mean(mtcars$mpg), 1)
```

Write: "The dataset contains `` `r knitr::inline_expr("n_cars")` `` cars with an average fuel efficiency of `` `r knitr::inline_expr("avg_mpg")` `` mpg."

Result: The dataset contains `r n_cars` cars with an average fuel efficiency of `r avg_mpg` mpg.

If your data changes, these numbers update automatically!

# Figures and Tables

## Labeled Figures

Give figures labels and captions for cross-referencing:

```{r}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between horsepower and fuel efficiency"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = hp, y = mpg, color = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Horsepower", y = "Miles per Gallon", color = "Cylinders") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Reference it in text with `@fig-scatter`: See @fig-scatter.

## Tables from Code

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Average MPG by number of cylinders"

library(dplyr)
mtcars %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  summarize(
    `Average MPG` = round(mean(mpg), 1),
    `Count` = n()
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

Reference with `@tbl-summary`: See @tbl-summary.

# Rendering Your Document

To create the final output:

1. **RStudio:** Click the "Render" button or press Ctrl+Shift+K
2. **Terminal:** Run `quarto render yourfile.qmd`

The output (`.html`, `.pdf`, etc.) appears in the same folder.
